KEY MESSAGE 1...
High pressure remains near southern Quebec this morning bringing 
one more cool morning with lows in the mid 30s to mid 40s, as 
some cirrus stream in. Some patchy fog in the sheltered valleys 
will burn off. Most of the day will remain dry with temps 
rebounding into the 60s to even lower 70s in some of the valley 
areas, as high clouds increase. Clouds will thicken and lower 
south and east of the Capital Region towards sunset. 
North/northeast winds will be breezy throughout the day with 
some gusts 20-30 mph, as the sfc pressure gradient tightens 
between the anticyclone to the north and the low pressure system
organizing east of the Mid Atlantic Region over the western 
Atlantic Ocean. A Wind Advisory was started at 2 pm today for 
Litchfield Co., CT, but the greatest gusts will likely occur 
late tonight through Saturday.

KEY MESSAGE 2...
Low pressure will rapidly intensify into the Nor'easter that 
will impact the forecast area tonight through the better part of
the weekend. The ensembles, medium range guidance, CAMS, and 
AI-GFS/AI-ECMWF all show the storm impacting portions of Long 
Island and the Northeast this weekend, but there continues to be
a variation in the timing of the deep low pressure system 
initially deepening into the 980-985 hPa range. The Nor'easter 
initially has an inverted sfc trough that will bring some rain 
into the region tonight, especially south and east of the 
Capital Region. The Nor'easter initially is moving north/northwest.
Some rain spreads northwest of the system along its deformation
zone on Saturday. The CAMS such as the 3-km HRRR and NAMnest 
are slow bringing the rain into locations from Albany north and 
west by Saturday. This due to the storm beginning to drift west 
or even west/southwest due to the blocking high to the north and
the Nor'easter being closed off. The latest EC/GFS/CMC/GEFS 
mean also have the storm begin moving westward by late Saturday 
pm, which may occur south of Long Island and drift towards the 
NJ Coast. 

The areal extent of the rainfall is challenging due to 
where the storm tracks. Locations south and east of the Capital 
Region have the best chance to receive the most rain. There is a
general consensus with the guidance that the rain shield
increases across the forecast area late Sat night into Sun.
Highest PoPs in the 60-85% range are used from the
northern/eastern Catskills/Capital Region/southern VT south and
east. An anomalous low-level north/northeast jet will be
advecting Atlantic moisture. PWATS rise above normal, but again
there could be a sharp cut-off in the rainfall north and west of
Albany. Temps will run cooler than normal on Sunday with mid 50s
to lower 60s on Sunday. The Nor'easter meanders towards the NJ
Coast/Delmarva Region potentially late Sunday, then does a loop
around and lifts back towards southeast New England Long Island
Mon into Tue. Drier weather would return by Tue.

Some variability will continue with the rainfall depending on
the track. From tonight into Monday morning rainfall totals are
projected to be a quarter inch or less over the western Mohawk
Valley, southern Adirondacks and Lake George area. Totals
increase from about a third of an inch to an inch over the
eastern Mohawk Valley, Saratoga Region and the Capital District.
1-2" are possible over the eastern Catskills, mid Hudson 
Valley, Taconics, southern VT, Berkshires and CW CT. The highest
amounts are expected across portions of NW CT and close to the
I-84. Latest NBM probs for > 1.0" of rain in the 48-hr period 
ending 8 AM Mon are now 35-80% from the Capital District south 
and east with the highest probs in the eastern Catskills, mid 
Hudson Valley and NW CT, and the >2" probs are 25-50% and are 
the highest in the eastern Catskills, southern Berkshires, 
southern Taconics, mid Hudson Valley and NW CT. Rivers are not 
expected to flood with 1-2" of rainfall over a 48-hr period. Dry
antecedent conditions should prevent flooding, outside ponding 
of water on roads and urban/poor drainage flooding of low- 
level lying areas. There could be a brief period of minor tidal 
flooding along the Hudson River at Poughkeepsie Sat evening into
early Sunday. If the storm track varies/deviates and is more 
northward, than higher QPF could yield some minor hydro 
concerns.

After collaboration with WFO OKX, we placed Litchfield County,
CT in a Wind Advisory for some gusts 40-50 mph late today into 
Sunday morning. North/northeast winds increase on the 
northwest/north side of the Nor'easter due to the tight low- 
level horizontal pressure gradient. The H850 low-level jet 
increases from the N/NE at 40-60 KT along and south and east of 
the Region. An inversion in the 850-750 hPa layer should 
prevent gusts from exceeding 25-40 mph over most of the region.
